key_insight: A provably sample-efficient, model-free robust Q-learning algorithm learns from a single Markovian trajectory while accounting for transition uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a principled approach to mitigating sim-to-real transition mismatches without explicitly learning a transition model.
method: Formulate a discounted robust MDP with total-variation uncertainty level σ.
Use asynchronous Q-learning on a single trajectory generated by a behavior policy under nominal transitions.
Prove sample-complexity guarantees for entrywise ε-approximation of the optimal robust Q-function.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical sample-complexity bound that improves prior bounds and is nearly minimax optimal up to an additional factor of 1/(1−γ); it describes no empirical evaluation.
watch_item: Sample requirements worsen with poor state-action coverage, slow trajectory mixing, and discount factors near one.
paper_title: Provably Efficient Q-learning for Robust Reinforcement Learning
